## Decompose: Unsigned slices

[**The Ozaki scheme:** **Decompose** → Multiply → Accumulate]{style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #666"}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="62%"}
![](../figures/static/slides/esc_slice_d3.svg){height="480px"}
:::

::: {.column width="38%"}
::: fragment
Only the first slice carries sign information, so every bit in the other slices holds mantissa bits.
:::
:::
:::::

## Automatic Dynamic Precision (ADP)

[**ADP:** Wraps Decompose → Multiply → Accumulate]{style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #666"}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](../figures/papers/schwarz/fig08.png){height="470px"}
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
::: {style="font-size: 0.8em"}
::: fragment
Check for Inf/NaN, compute ESC, then decide: emulate, or fall back to native DGEMM
:::

<br>

::: fragment
**Goal:** A matrix product at least as accurate as native FP64, in at least the same amount of time
:::

<br>

::: fragment
How the heuristic decides "emulation slower than FP64?" is not described.
:::
:::
:::
:::::

## Moving away from the error-free guarantee

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Ozaki et al. (2012)**

Goal: As little rounding error as possible

Slice width $\alpha$ chosen so slice products are provably exact
:::

::: {.column .fragment width="50%"}
**Schwarz et al. (2026)**

Goal: FP64-equivalent accuracy

Slices always contain eight significant bits; ESC sets how many slices are needed
:::
:::::

<br>

::: fragment
**The only evidence that this maintains FP64-equivalent accuracy is their empirical evaluation.**
:::

**With fallback:** Accuracy indistinguishable from native DGEMM. Speedup grows with problem size.

## Impacts of implementation

::: fragment
**Performance:** Consistent with Ootomo et al., but ESC adds overhead that doesn't become negligible even at the largest sizes
:::

<br>

::: fragment
**Usability:** Users never have to consider the magnitude range of their inputs or the throughputs of their hardware...
:::

::: fragment
... but this critical piece of enabling safe emulation remains a black box
:::
